questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how TopicSubscriptions uses its read-write lock when adding a subscriber? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
subscribersOf() returns a new ArrayList rather than the internal set. What does that mean for publish() when a user unsubscribes during delivery?
choices: publish() throws ConcurrentModificationException because the underlying set changed.
Unsubscribing blocks until the in-flight publish has finished its loop.
The unsubscribe is invisible to the in-progress publish, so the user may still receive that message.
The user is removed from the loop immediately, so no further sends occur for them.

questions.prompt: Under steady traffic with many publishers and occasional unsubscribes, how do concurrent publish() calls interact at the registry?
choices: They run strictly one after another because every access goes through the same ReentrantReadWriteLock.
They can look up subscribers at the same time, and only wait while an unsubscribe holds the write lock.
They never wait for anything, since reads are lock-free.
They block each other during the sending phase, because the lock is held for the whole publish.

questions.prompt: One recipient's sender.send() throws an exception partway through the list. What does publish() return?
choices: The exception propagates and the remaining recipients are not notified.
A Result with zero deliveries, since a partial failure aborts the batch.
The call retries the failed recipient until it succeeds.
A Result with the failure counted, after the remaining recipients have still been attempted.
